title: Spirituality and Religion Compared
excerpt: Religion usually adds shared ritual, authority, and history. Spirituality sometimes names the private side of that life and sometimes a life outside it.

quick_answer.question: What is the difference between spirituality and religion?
quick_answer.answer: Religion usually names communities, rituals, authorities, and a history. Spirituality often names personal meaning or practice, either inside a religion or apart from one. Neither word is automatically deeper.

intro: The sentence I am spiritual but not religious is common in the United States. It can mean a real distance from institutions. It can also mean the institutions were edited out while their practices were kept.

sections.heading: What does religion add?
sections.content:
A congregation, a calendar, a text read with others, and a person who can say no are typical religious pieces. Spirituality, as used on this site, is the wider and vaguer word for meaning and practice. It is not a promotion.

The neighboring page is [what spirituality is](/articles/what-is-spirituality/). Treat that link as part of the argument, not as decoration.

sections.heading: Why do Americans split the words?
sections.content:
A Protestant stress on inner sincerity shapes the split, and so does the late twentieth-century market in Asian practices sold as personal growth. Ancient wisdom pages put the community and the book back where a quote removed them.

A wider map lives at the [spirituality topic](/topics/spirituality/). Dates and school names matter, because a recent American presentation is often described as if it had no date.

sections.heading: What mistake follows the split?
sections.content:
You can pray inside a religion and call it spiritual. You can meditate outside a religion and still be borrowing a religious technique. Say which you are doing. The starting guide does not require you to leave a tradition.

If you want a narrower practical or comparative page, use [starting a practice](/articles/starting-a-spiritual-practice/). You can understand the description without joining a group or buying a course.

sections.heading: What should a careful reader refuse?
sections.content:
Do not use spiritual as a way to avoid criticism, refunds, or medical care. Institutions can be corrupt. So can a teacher with no institution. The word you prefer does not settle the ethics.

Readers in the United States often meet a simpler version of the same idea in a class, an app, or a short video. Name that simpler version instead of pretending it is the whole tradition. Traditional teaching, personal report, and research stay in separate sentences on this site. The [editorial policy](/editorial-policy/) is the rule. The [disclaimer](/disclaimer/) applies whenever a sentence leans toward health, safety, or a promised transformation. The [corrections](/corrections/) page is how to challenge a factual mistake. Name the school, the text, or the century whenever a sentence would otherwise float free of history. A reader may stop at the definition when that is all the question required.

key_takeaways: Religion usually implies a shared form of life.
Spirituality is a broader and less precise word.
One is not more evolved than the other.

faq.question: Can a person be both?
faq.answer: Yes. Many people use spiritual language for the inner side of a religion they still practice.

faq.question: Where is the overview?
faq.answer: Use the spirituality pillar and the guide hub.
